title: "Part 4 – Robustness"
---

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../live/day.html#/part-4-robustness){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 4 turns from the reproduction of one analysis to robustness, the second of the three Rs. The specification menu is taken apart decision by decision, you explore it and send the analysis that you would defend to the class chart, and the class reads its chart against the curve of 864 specifications of the claim. The part then asks what the curve establishes and what a replication of the claim would have to fix in advance, and it closes on the analysis that you preregister before running it.

## 1. The specification menu

**On the slides**, with the specification menu open in another tab.

[Open the specification menu](../../menu.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The slides take you through the fourteen decisions, the three groups into which they sort, the options that the curve of 864 keeps and what Task 2 of the robustness study of SCORE (Multi100; Aczel et al. 2026) left open. The slides end on the ground rules for the menu and on the convention of claim alignment. Every decision starts from the reproduced specification, the model of C6HJR, whichever analyst you reproduced.

## 2. The methods behind the menu

**On the slides.** An optional tutorial takes the methods behind the decisions of the menu, a slide or two for each, and the facilitator switches it on or off.

## 3. Task 4 – The menu

[Open the deck at Task 4](../../live/day.html#/hands-on-4-work-the-menu){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Open the browser lab at Task 4](../../lab.qmd#task-4-explore){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

In the workspace, work through Task 4 of `index.qmd`, from the chunk `try-baseline` to the chunk `submit-exploration`, or the section on Task 4 of `working_script.R`. Call `try_spec()` three or four times, changing one argument at a time, and print the tries side by side with `my_experiments()`. Then submit the one that you would defend with `submit_exploration()`. Your dot is drawn on the [class chart](../../class-results.qmd) as an exploratory result. The deck shows each step with its output on the slides of Hands-on 4, and with the browser lab it carries the task if your installation fails.

## 4. The multiverse

**On the slides.** The slides name what you did in Task 4, your own small multiverse, and an optional run says where the idea comes from, with the garden of forking paths drawn, the filters for inclusion, enumeration against curation and the purposes that a multiverse can serve.

To go further: [The multiverse and its critics](../../companion/multiverse.qmd).

## 5. The class chart and the curve

**On the slides**, with the Class results page open in another tab.

[Open the Class results page](../../class-results.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The exploratory dots of the class are set against the curve of 864. You place a bet in the chat on which decision moves the estimates most, before the slides show the decomposition. The slides then place the five reanalyses and the original study on the curve, and show what the options off the curve do to it.

## 6. Your placement

[Open the deck at your placement](../../live/day.html#/find-your-own-percentile){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Open the browser lab at Task 4](../../lab.qmd#task-4-explore){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

Rerun the specification that you submitted with `try_spec()`, in the console of your IDE or in the chunk `try-one-at-a-time`, read off your own placement among the 864 specifications of the curve, and send it in the chat when the facilitator says go. The deck shows the step on its slide of the placement. Without a submission of your own, use the placement of the reproduced specification, which is 67%.

## 7. Reading a specification curve

**On the slides**, with the reading on inference of the Specification curve page open in another tab.

[Open Inference on the curve](../../curve.qmd#inference){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The slides say what the curve leaves out, and separate the two jobs that a curve can do, description and inference. The slides show why the 864 estimates depend on one another and are not 864 tests, how a permutation design builds the distribution against which a curve-level test is read, and what stands without the test.

## 8. A replication of the claim

**On the slides.** The replication that SCORE ran on later waves of the Standard Eurobarometer returns with its verdict, and the slides ask what a replication of the analysis that you reproduced would have to decide before anyone opens the new data.

## 9. Critics and preregistration

**On the slides.** The slides present the three critical positions on multiverse analysis and the argument that a fully specified question has one correct analysis, with the question of how anyone would identify it. The slides end on what preregistration settles and what it leaves open, and set the exploration of Task 4 against the declaration of Task 5.

## 10. Archives and registrations

**On the slides.** The slides show where a reanalysis is archived and registered, the three OSF addresses of the case study, the SCORE dossier, the preregistration of the robustness study itself and the two preregistration templates, and they map the eight AsPredicted questions onto the decisions that you have already met.

To go further: [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd).

## 11. Task 5 – The preregistration

[Open the deck at Task 5](../../live/day.html#/the-preregistration-moment){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Open the browser lab at Task 5](../../lab.qmd#task-5-my-preregistration){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

In the workspace, complete the preregistration block of `index.qmd`, the chunk `prereg`, before you run anything, then run it, which calls `prereg()`, render the report, and type "declared" in the chat. When the class has declared, go on to the chunks `build-model`, `run-spec` and `report`: translate the declaration into model syntax yourself, run it, and submit it with `report_result()`. Your result is drawn on the chart as a declared one beside the exploratory round. The deck shows each step with its output on the slides of Hands-on 5, and if your installation fails, the deck carries the task, as does the browser lab, in its preregistration and its section [build, run and report](../../lab.qmd#task-5-build-run-report).

## 12. The close

**On the slides**, with the [class chart](../../class-results.qmd) on screen. The day closes on two points from the literature, the single analytical path, what you take with you, and the feedback form.
